summary: Incumbent Democratic Sen. Chris Coons ran for reelection and won, defeating Republican Michael Katz.

candidates.name: Chris Coons
candidates.bio: Democratic U.S. senator from Delaware, first elected in 2010. He won the 2026 Democratic primary with nearly 80% of the vote and serves on the Senate Small Business Committee. His campaign slogan is "Make Washington More Like Delaware."

positions.summary: Sits on the Senate Small Business Committee, has introduced legislation to expand apprenticeships, and says a college degree should not be required for a well-paying job.
Says every American deserves access to quality, affordable health care.
Co-led the bipartisan Afghan Adjustment Act and championed the NO BAN Act.
Says he wants Delaware to be a hub of clean energy technology and has secured federal funding for the Mid-Atlantic Clean Hydrogen Hub and coastal resilience projects.
Supports the Reproductive Freedom for Women Act, which would put Roe v. Wade's protections into federal law, and the Right to Contraception Act.

candidates.name: Michael Katz
candidates.bio: Anesthesiologist and commercial real estate company owner who served in the Delaware State Senate as a Democrat from 2009 to 2013. He ran for U.S. Senate with the Independent Party in 2024 and as a Republican in 2026. He won the Republican primary with about 77% of the vote.

positions.summary: Would cut federal programs he sees as "job killing" and make pro-growth tax cuts permanent, according to a WHYY voter guide.
Calls the Affordable Care Act "a failed policy" overall and has called for repealing it, while saying it has "a lot of really good things in it," including protections for pre-existing conditions.
Favors border security, withholding funding from sanctuary jurisdictions and enforcing stricter immigration laws, according to a WHYY voter guide.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35). Official count: the state results index lists "General Election Official Results", and the state data table "Official Election Results by Office" gives Coons 240,587 and Katz 137,837. Shares include the 1,330 write-ins in the state's official write-in report. The state results file for the 2026 General Election is marked "OFFICIAL RESULTS".
